tools.name: search_rulings
tools.description: Search published employment-law rulings from our research corpus by keyword, law, court, federal circuit, state, outcome, and date. Returns published opinions with citations, outcomes, procedural stage, employers, claim types, recorded monetary amounts, and links to the full opinion. Use this to ground any claim about how employment cases have been decided. Results are quality-filtered (low-confidence and junk rows excluded).

query.description: Lexical search across case name, opinion excerpt, stored summary and employer. Every word must match; a match does not verify a claim or holding.

law.description: Filter by a stored law association (not a verified holding), e.g. "title-vii", "adea", "ada", "fmla", "flsa".

court.description: Filter by CourtListener court id, e.g. "scotus", "ca11" (11th Circuit).

circuit.description: Filter to a federal appeals circuit (the appeals court plus its district courts). Preferred values: first-circuit, second-circuit, third-circuit, fourth-circuit, fifth-circuit, sixth-circuit, seventh-circuit, eighth-circuit, ninth-circuit, tenth-circuit, eleventh-circuit, dc-circuit, federal-circuit. Display forms like "Eleventh Circuit" or "11th" are also accepted.

state.description: US state or territory where the case was filed, by name or postal abbreviation (e.g. "Florida" or "FL").

outcome.description: Filter by the stored outcome label. On older rows that are not source-checked, plaintiff_win and defendant_win name the side of the case caption, not the worker or the employer; a matching row whose label the site withholds is returned with outcome_type null.

tools.name: find_similar_cases
tools.description: Provide a nonempty claim_types, protected_classes or law_ids array, or a value for employer_name, industry or state. Given the facts of an employment situation — claim types, protected class, employer, state — analyze how similar real cases in the corpus were decided. Returns the aggregate plaintiff win rate, settlement rate, typical damages range, the topics courts discussed most in opinions plaintiffs won vs. lost, and a few representative example cases. Win and loss counts come from stored outcome labels, which include older automated labels coded by the side of the case caption, so they are worded as plaintiff and defendant. Counts are returned at three levels (nationwide, the federal courts of the state's region, and the state) with a detailed breakdown for one level: who won, award amounts, what happened at each stage, and topics. Every figure is labeled with the level it describes. A level with few opinions returns counts without a win rate. Each example says what happened and why it matched. Topic rows record what opinions discussed, not what courts found. These are educational statistics from published opinions: a historical percentage is not any one person’s probability of winning, and the results are not a prediction or legal advice. In structured stages: won and wonPct count opinions the plaintiff won in whole or in part (wonPct leaves rulings sent back out of its base), and sentBack counts rulings sent back to a lower court. wentForward and wentForwardPct include rulings sent back to a lower court and are kept for compatibility.

claim_types.description: Claim types alleged, e.g. ["retaliation","wrongful termination","discrimination","harassment"]. The single highest-value signal.

employer_name.description: Employer / defendant name, e.g. "Union Pacific Railroad". Used for a fuzzy match.

state.description: US state name or postal abbreviation where the situation arose, e.g. "Florida" or "FL".

law_ids.description: Related law ids, federal or state, e.g. ["title-vii","adea","ada","fmla","flsa","fl-fcra","ca-feha"].

level.description: Which level the detailed breakdown and examples describe: "national" (default), "circuit" (federal courts of the state's region), or "state". All three levels' counts are returned either way.

narrow_to_laws.description: Only count opinions that mention one of law_ids (a federal law or its state analogue). Default false: every opinion sharing the claim type, under any law.

inputSchema.description: Provide a nonempty claim_types, protected_classes or law_ids array, or a value for employer_name, industry or state.

tools.name: get_employer_track_record
tools.description: Given an employer/company name, return distinct federal cases and trusted published employment opinions that involve that employer, the breakdown of outcomes (employee wins, employer wins, settlements, dismissals), the most notable recent opinions, AND the count of federal docket records on file (cases that may not have a written opinion). Use this when a user names their employer and wants that company's litigation history + footprint.

employer.description: Employer/company name to look up, e.g. "Walmart", "Acme Corporation". Common suffixes like Inc/Corp/LLC are ignored when matching.

limit.description: Number of example published opinions to return (1–25). The total count and outcome breakdown reflect the full corpus, not just these examples.

tools.name: get_attorney_track_record
tools.description: Given an employment attorney name (or profile slug), return the federal employment-law cases on file in which that attorney appeared — case caption, court, year, nature-of-suit, and the side they appeared for when on record. Use this when a user names an attorney and wants their public litigation history. Facts only, sourced from federal court dockets. Attorney identities are algorithmically matched; ambiguous and lower-confidence matches are excluded. One case is one normalized court+docket number, so duplicate source rows do not inflate the count.

attorney.description: Employment attorney full name (e.g. "Jane Doe") or their workers-rights.com profile slug.

limit.description: Number of example cases to return (1–25). Counts reflect all cases on file, not just these.

tools.name: explain_my_rights
tools.description: Provide a nonblank issue or protected_class, or both. Explain which federal (and state, if a state is given) employment laws may protect a worker based on the type of issue (e.g. discrimination, harassment, retaliation, wrongful termination) and/or the protected class involved (e.g. race, sex, age, disability, pregnancy). Returns the relevant statutes with citations, who they cover (employer-size thresholds), filing deadlines and agencies, and available remedies. Use this to ground an answer about a worker’s legal protections. Deadline guidance covers private-sector and state/local government workers; federal employees follow a separate process with a much shorter deadline (45 days to contact their agency's EEO counselor). Educational information, not legal advice.

employer_sector.description: Whether the employer is private, state/local government, or a federal agency.

issue.description: Type of workplace issue, e.g. "discrimination", "harassment", "retaliation", "wrongful termination", "unpaid wages", "disability accommodation".

state.description: US state (2-letter code or full name) to include state-specific protections and the correct EEOC filing deadline.

inputSchema.description: Provide a nonblank issue or protected_class, or both.

tools.name: get_eeoc_process
tools.description: Plain-English guide to the 9 stages of an EEOC discrimination/retaliation charge, from pre-filing through resolution. Call with no arguments for an overview of all stages with typical durations; call with a stage number (1-9) for a deep-dive on that stage: what to expect, how long it takes, the key tip, and do/don't guidance. Use this whenever someone asks what happens after filing with the EEOC, how long the process takes, what a position statement or rebuttal is, or what to do at the stage they are currently in. Covers private-sector and state/local government workers; federal employees follow a separate EEO process with a much shorter deadline (45 days to contact their agency's EEO counselor).

stage.description: Stage number 1-9 for a deep-dive on one stage. Omit for an overview of all nine stages.

tools.name: get_evidence_preservation_checklist
tools.description: Concrete checklist for a worker who senses termination coming or is in a deteriorating work situation: what to write down, which records are already theirs to gather (pay records, documents they were given), and how to list everything else so an attorney can ask the employer to preserve it. It does not advise copying or forwarding material from an employer’s systems. Use this whenever someone says they think they are about to be fired, fears retaliation is escalating, mentions a PIP or sudden access changes, or asks what to do before reporting discrimination. Sections: 'today' (highest-leverage, minutes matter), 'this-week', 'quiet' (low-priority prep). Time-sensitive — employers often revoke system access during the termination call itself.

group.description: Checklist section for a focused list: 'today' (highest-leverage, do first), 'this-week', or 'quiet' (lower-priority quiet prep). Omit for the full checklist.

tools.name: find_employment_attorney
tools.description: Provide a state, a known city or both lat and lng. Find public-source employment-law attorney listings near a US location. Returns source-attributed identity, firm, location, and contact data sorted by proximity. Person-specific filters and fields apply only where the underlying directory supports them; Google Places metrics are labeled as firm/office listing data, never individual ratings. Listings are not state-bar verification or an endorsement.

state.description: US state, e.g. "FL" or "Florida". Provide a state, a known city or a coordinate pair.

city.description: Optional city to tighten the search center (e.g. "Tampa").

lat.description: Latitude in degrees. Supply together with lng.

lng.description: Longitude in degrees. Supply together with lat.

language.description: Filter on attorney-supplied language data. Most listings are public office records that do not publish it; when none in range do, the tool returns total 0 with unsupported_filters rather than silently implying no attorneys are nearby.

min_rating.description: Minimum individual-profile rating. Office/business ratings are never treated as an attorney rating, so this matches only hand-managed profiles and returns nothing where none exist.

free_consultation.description: Filter on attorney-supplied fee data. Most listings are public office records that do not publish it; when none in range do, the tool returns total 0 with unsupported_filters rather than implying no attorneys are nearby.

contingency_fee.description: Filter on attorney-supplied fee data. Most listings are public office records that do not publish it; when none in range do, the tool returns total 0 with unsupported_filters rather than implying no attorneys are nearby.

radius_miles.description: Search radius. Defaults to 100mi for broad statewide coverage.

inputSchema.description: Provide a state, a known city or both lat and lng.

tools.name: get_corpus_stats
tools.description: Return live statistics about the Workers' Rights corpus: total number of collected court records in the research corpus, number of public attorney listings, number of monitored legal data sources, the date the corpus was last updated, and the distribution of reportable outcomes before the employment browse filter. Use this to establish scale/credibility or to answer 'how much data do you have / how current is it'.
